Accessibility

Source: vignettes/articles/accessibility.Rmd
accessibility.Rmd

accessibility() summarises, for each origin, how many opportunities (jobs, schools, hospitals…) can be reached, either counting those within a time limit or weighting every one of them by how long it takes to get there. The travel times come from the same computation as travel_time_matrix().

Two details of the computation: the travel time fed to the decay function is the percentile in seconds, not rounded to minutes as in the matrix, and the exponentials are computed with Apache Commons Math’s FastMath.exp algorithm, not with the C library’s, so the values do not depend on the platform’s maths library.

Cumulative opportunities

The "step" function counts the opportunities reached in less than each cutoff. Each origin gets one row per opportunity column, percentile and cutoff:

access <- accessibility(
  network, points, points,
  opportunities_colnames = c("jobs", "schools"),
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  departure_datetime = departure,
  decay_function = "step",
  cutoffs = c(15, 30),
  percentiles = c(25, 75),
  seed = 42,
  n_threads = 2
)
head(access, 8)
#> # A tibble: 8 × 5
#>   id              opportunity percentile cutoff accessibility
#>   <chr>           <chr>            <int>  <int>         <dbl>
#> 1 89a8100c00fffff jobs                25     15         12452
#> 2 89a8100c00fffff jobs                25     30         95249
#> 3 89a8100c00fffff jobs                75     15         12452
#> 4 89a8100c00fffff jobs                75     30         81835
#> 5 89a8100c00fffff schools             25     15             1
#> 6 89a8100c00fffff schools             25     30             4
#> 7 89a8100c00fffff schools             75     15             1
#> 8 89a8100c00fffff schools             75     30             4

With "step", trips longer than the largest cutoff are not routed at all (max_trip_duration becomes max(cutoffs)), and max_trip_duration may not be shorter than the largest cutoff with any function.

Decay functions

The other functions weight every opportunity by its travel time. Their decay_value means different things: the width of the ramp in minutes for "linear", the standard deviation in minutes for "logistic", the decay constant per second for "fixed_exponential"; "exponential" uses the cutoff as its half-life.

one <- function(fun, value = NULL, cutoffs = 20) {
  a <- accessibility(
    network, points[1:3, ], points,
    opportunities_colnames = "jobs",
    mode = "WALK",
    decay_function = fun, decay_value = value, cutoffs = cutoffs,
    n_threads = 2
  )
  setNames(round(a$accessibility), a$id)
}
rbind(
  step = one("step"),
  exponential = one("exponential"),
  linear = one("linear", 10),
  logistic = one("logistic", 5),
  fixed_exponential = one("fixed_exponential", 0.001, cutoffs = NULL)
)
#>                   89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c007ffff 89a8100c077ffff
#> step                        16948           24325           31926
#> exponential                 42932           45737           48674
#> linear                      18205           22571           29017
#> logistic                    20363           25331           31449
#> fixed_exponential           23096           25598           28264

"fixed_exponential" ignores cutoffs, so cutoffs must be NULL and the result has no cutoff column.

Street modes

Any street mode works too; the times are then the same for every percentile.

by_bike <- accessibility(
  network, points, points,
  opportunities_colnames = "jobs",
  mode = "BICYCLE",
  decay_function = "logistic", decay_value = 5, cutoffs = 15,
  n_threads = 2
)
summary(by_bike$accessibility)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   27175   65097   85186   78586   94017  102146

Missing counts

Missing opportunity counts count as zero, with a warning:

holes <- points
holes$jobs[2] <- NA
a <- accessibility(network, points[1, ], holes,
                   opportunities_colnames = "jobs", mode = "WALK",
                   decay_function = "step", cutoffs = 30, n_threads = 2)
#> Warning: `jobs` has 1 missing value, treated as 0.
a
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   id              opportunity percentile cutoff accessibility
#>   <chr>           <chr>            <int>  <int>         <dbl>
#> 1 89a8100c00fffff jobs                50     30         57664
